full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff is the appellant. He filed a suit for declaration of his title and for recovery of khas possession. The suit was decreed by the trial Court but on appeal the lower appellate court dismissed the suit on reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court. His second Appeal was dismissed summarily by a learned Single Judge of the High Court. 

 5. The plaintiff pressed his case with regard to c.s. plot Nos. 9072 and 90/5. The trial Court accepted his case and decreed the suit. The appellate Court below in a well-considered judgment came to the conclusion that plot No. 9075 being a pathway the plaintiff was not entitled to any relief. So the only question is whether the plaintiff had put his case so far as the plot No. 9072 is concerned. Possession of the land was considered as a deciding factor for adjudication. It was noticed that excepting the recital in Exhibit 1 there is no other proof that. Bidban Bibi acquired 16 annas interest in the disputed land. No. evidence was led that the Kbajanchi Bari landlords possessed the disputed land in khas. The plaintiff's case is that he was in possession and he leased out the plot to Jainab Bibi and then himself purchased the right of Jainab Bibi does not stand scrutiny because the evidence is that Exhibit 1 shows that the defendant was given permission for construction on 31.5 1965 whereas the permission for construction to the plaintiff is-dated 21.6.1965. The appellate Court below noticed that the permission of the defendant for construction of the shed is prior to that of Jainab Bibi. Oral evidence was considered and the conclusion was that there was no disinterested witness to establish the claim of possession of the plaintiff in the disputed land. Exhibit C which is the judgment in objection case showed that the plot No. 9072 has been recorded in name of the defendant, as the tenant under the plaintiff. It was concluded that the rent receiving interest having been acquired the plaintiff ceased to have any interest in the disputed land. Exhibit 2 khatian has been recorded in the name of the defendants. Exhibit F is the report of the Advocate Commissioner of local inspection which showed that the defendant was in possession of the disputed plot living there with his family and growing vegetables. Exhibit C is dated 18.5.1957. The plaintiff's case was that he leased out to Jainab Bibi on 7.2.1953 and again purchased it on. 2.10.1965. Exhibit C of the judgment belies his stand. Moreover, no cogent evidence was given to show that the plaintiff paid any consideration for the kabala. Exhibit 1(b) by which lie purchased the property from Jainab Bibi. On the other hand, Exhibit B series shows that the defendant had been paying municipal dues for the land in question and Exhibit E shows payment of rent to the Government by the defendant. Survey settlement record shows that the defendant was in possession of the disputed plot during the settlement operation. That was in 1954. It was concluded and correctly so that the defendant was in possession from before. Therefore, the plaintiff having failed to establish his possession in the suit land within 12 years from the institution of the suit he is not entitled to get any relief, the suit being barred by limitation. This conclusion is in accordance with law. The High Court Division had summarily dismissed the appeal. In all fairness it must be stated in the case of judgment of reversal, justice demands a consideration of the materials which led to the reversal of the trial court judgment and the reasons which weighed heavily warranting summary dismissal of the Second Appeal. Conclusions reached by the Appellate Court below in this Case are correct and the plaintiff failed to show that he was in possession of the disputed land within 12 years from the date of institution of the suit. That being the position the reversal of the trial court judgment by the appellate Court below was justified and the plaintiff is not entitled to any relief. In the result therefore, this appeal is dismissed with cost.
